name: marching-arts
description: Placeholder name. Authorization core for a marching-program platform — per-record bands, sealed grants, and a resolver that compiles to one SQL predicate.
author: USER

data_streams.purpose: Records about members, each carrying a classification band and a provenance string
data_streams.retention: undetermined — varies by band and by jurisdiction; see notes.retention
data_streams.description: On-device only. Never leaves the process; no export path exists rather than a disabled one.

data_streams.purpose: Consent grants — who may see whose information, and to what band
data_streams.description: Only a grant a named human sealed authorizes anything. Revocation deletes rather than flags, so no residue of a former grant is readable.

data_streams.purpose: Roster identity and birthdate — the input to whether a member is a minor
data_streams.description: A birthdate rather than an is_minor flag: a flag is true until somebody remembers to run the job that clears it. On-device only.

data_streams.purpose: Which adult holds guardian authority over which minor
data_streams.description: Names a second person who is not themselves a member. A guardian is the only party who may seal a grant they benefit from, and that authority expires at majority rather than persisting.

data_streams.purpose: Hash-chained consent and disclosure log, with a count anchor
data_streams.description: Append-only and tamper-evident. The count anchor is what detects tail truncation, which a plain chain cannot. Chain names do not carry the subject id. Readable only by the subject and parties entitled to it; a non-entitled reader gets an empty list rather than a refusal, so probing the log cannot distinguish a member who declined from one who does not exist.

notes.name: Generic placeholder. Directory name is the app_id while in the playground; a promoted app gets its own repo and its own identity.
notes.not_stored_here: Band 5 (safeguarding) is never served by this app to anyone under any grant. Concerns are routed to the people whose job it is.
notes.retention: NOT YET DECIDED, and deliberately not declared as 'permanent' — which is what this manifest said until it was checked. Three things have to be settled first, and none is an engineering call. (1) Published youth-sector retention runs OPPOSITE to privacy intuition: a minor's limitation period often does not start until 18, and comparable bodies keep health records to majority-plus-years and abuse-related records for decades. A single 'delete the member' control is therefore wrong in one direction and 'keep forever' is wrong in the other. (2) The bands do not share a period or even a direction, so retention is per-band, not per-app. (3) FERPA does not attach to a 501(c)(3), but the high-school half of the stated market may drag it in indirectly, and the SOPIPA trigger is 'designed and marketed for K-12' — so a marketing decision carries a statutory one. Until counsel answers, the honest declaration is that this is open.
notes.deletion: Deletion and tamper-evidence are reconcilable and currently only half-built. The consent chain is partitioned per subject (migration 004), so one member's chain can be dropped without breaking anyone else's, and a dropped chain reads as absent rather than as tampered. Not yet done: content redaction WITHIN a surviving chain, which needs the chain to commit to a SALTED commitment H(salt||payload) with payload and salt in a separate deletable table. The salt is load-bearing — the action vocabulary is four strings and detail is member-ids plus a 0-6 integer, so an unsalted commitment over a 150-member corps is brute-forceable on a laptop.
